key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power governs penetration and keyhole growth, welding speed reduces weld dimensions, and current strengthens convection and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld penetration, width, and arc-stability control when fabricating Invar molds for aerospace composites.
method: Parameter analysis: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min welding speed, and 150–170 A current.
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, higher power increased penetration and arc deflection tendency, higher speed reduced penetration and width while increasing flow velocity and cooling rate, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract provides parameter trends but no quantitative prediction errors or weld-quality metrics, limiting assessment of model accuracy and production readiness.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
